name: attently
description: Gross-to-subtle communication for AI assistants. The depth contract and rendering rules from Vipassana meditation applied to how AI responds: verdict first, structure over prose, depth on demand. Inside cmux, the ring ranks every Claude session against your ~/.claude/attently/today.md so only what needs you reaches you, and invites day-phase rituals when you turn up. Blocks nothing. Reads today.md, areas.md (folder to area names), zenborg's phaseConfigs.json, each session's git branch and transcript ai-title / custom-title / last-prompt, the cmux tree and each turn's last message; when a session's topic moves, sends its ai-title, last prompt, marker and reply tail to Haiku (claude -p) for a tab name; names tabs and unnamed workspaces; stores session cards, saved descriptions and titles, and a ritual log under ~/.claude/attently/ring/ and ~/.claude/attently/. With a Claude Code build that loads mods, a hooks module carries the contract as a system-prompt section (the shell hooks' contract text then stands down), a band above the prompt with your configured replies, read feedback (which linked wiki pages you opened, told to Claude with your next typed prompt) and a /ring pane. The module reads the plugin's contract/, linked .claude/attently/*.md pages and ~/.claude/attently/ring/sessions/*.json; writes each session's card there (session, cwd, state, marker, ts); and sends a close-up message to a session only when you press its button.

replies.title: Turn band replies
replies.description: The replies the band above the prompt offers after a turn, separated by ·. A press submits that text.
replies.default: Close up · Commit and push · Go ahead
